Agent Name: Planner  
Step Number: 16  
Reason for Mistake: The Planner made an error by incorrectly determining the death year of Alexander the Great as 322 BCE. This mistake occurred due to a misunderstanding of how different year notations (civic and astronomical) are used in historical references. The normalization from 323/322 BCE to 322 BCE was incorrect because the task was asking for commonly cited historical facts, not an astronomical conversion. The correct year, widely accepted by historians, is 323 BCE, as verified by various reputable sources throughout the conversation steps. This mistake falls under the example pattern of using incorrect data conflation, similar to error types that involve confusion in conversion or fact-checking processes (see Example 3).
